It does feel like a good time, what with a new Harry Potter TV show on the way. The series' arrival on the 2026 TV schedule will likely spark even more interest than usual in the franchise, and possibly encourage a lot of millennials craving nostalgia to see Grint back as Ron.

It should be fun, especially given what Ron Weasley is up to in Harry Potter and the Cursed Child . articles.title: Ray Gunn's Brad Bird Reveals the Biggest Film Noir Influence on New Netflix Movie [EXCLUSIVE]
articles.summary: Brad Bird's Ray Gunn may look like something out of a 1930s science fiction magazine, but its titular detective owes quite a bit to Jack Nicholson. The director of The Iron Giant and The Incredibles is finally making the animated detective movie he's been trying to make for decades. While Bird drew inspiration from Humphrey […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Brad Bird's Ray Gunn may look like something out of a 1930s science fiction magazine, but its titular detective owes quite a bit to Jack Nicholson. The director of The Iron Giant and The Incredibles is finally making the animated detective movie he's been trying to make for decades . While Bird drew inspiration from Humphrey Bogart's detective movies, it was Jack Nicholson's performance in a 1970s neo-noir that helped shape the character of Ray Gunn.

Speaking exclusively with ComicBook's Chris Killian, Bird revealed that Roman Polanski's Chinatown was a big influence on the character of Ray Gunn. In particular, Bird loves what Nicholson was willing to do as an actor to sell the story of private detective J.J. Gittes. "In terms of character, I mean, for me, I love The Maltese Falcon and The Big Sleep with Bogart," Bird explained. "But to me, the best detective movie ever made is Chinatown ."

Bird singled out Nicholson's decision to spend much of Chinatown with a bandage on his nose. "He's snoopy and he's sticking the nose where it shouldn't be, and the nose actually pays the price," Bird explained. "And the lack of vanity he had of going through that movie with this just honking bandage on his nose is just… that's great filmmaking." While Nicholson informed the character, another Hollywood icon inspired his appearance. "Physically, we kind of looked at young Montgomery Clift," Bird revealed. "He kind of has striking eyebrows and a very interesting face."

Perhaps the most obvious comparison to Ray Gunn is Robert Zemeckis' Who Framed Roger Rabbit . Both movies take the classic private detective story and have some fun with the genre by populating their worlds with characters that could only exist through animation. In the case of Ray Gunn , it's aliens and robots rather than cartoon characters. Who Framed Roger Rabbit also got away with quite a bit for a PG-rated movie. Between the murder investigation at the center of the story and Jessica Rabbit 's relationship with her husband, there's plenty in the movie that plays differently for adults than it does for kids.

Bird has spent much of his career challenging the idea that animated movies are inherently children's entertainment. The Incredibles is as much a movie about a man going through a midlife crisis and struggling with his marriage as it is a superhero movie. And while Bird has yet to direct an R-rated animated feature, he told ComicBook that he'd be open to making one if the right story came along.

With Ray Gunn , Bird is getting the opportunity to make the kind of animated movie he rarely gets to see himself. Hopefully, its success will afford him and other filmmakers more opportunities to explore genres that Hollywood has largely reserved for live-action movies. If Bird does get to make an R-rated animated movie, let's hope it doesn't take another 30 years. Ray Gunn arrives in select theaters on December 4th and premieres on Netflix on December 18th.

articles.title: Buffy Once Made a Thanksgiving Episode That Was Much More Controversial Than Fans Remember
articles.summary: The late '90s were a pretty wonderful time to be a television fan. Friends was dominating Thursday nights, The X-Files was still making people afraid of perfectly ordinary forests, and every network seemed determined to find the next big supernatural hit. Meanwhile, Buffy the Vampire Slayer was busy proving that a show about a teenage […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google The late '90s were a pretty wonderful time to be a television fan. Friends was dominating Thursday nights, The X-Files was still making people afraid of perfectly ordinary forests, and every network seemed determined to find the next big supernatural hit. Meanwhile, Buffy the Vampire Slayer was busy proving that a show about a teenage girl fighting vampires could be considerably smarter than its premise suggested. It also had a habit of making ordinary occasions extremely dangerous. Apparently, not even Thanksgiving was safe.

There's something particularly entertaining about revisiting holiday episodes from this era. They remind us of a time when television characters actually had to show up at somebody's house for dinner instead of sending a group text. But one of Buffy's holiday adventures deserves a closer look for reasons that have little to do with turkey or awkward family conversations. The fourth season tackled a particularly uncomfortable part of American history and wrapped it in a supernatural adventure. It wasn't exactly the sort of Thanksgiving special you'd expect between Home Improvement reruns and a football game.

That episode was " Pangs " from November 1999. Buffy wants to celebrate Thanksgiving with her friends, but a construction project awakens the spirit of a Chumash warrior named Hus. He's understandably furious about the treatment of his people and has no intention of quietly accepting the holiday festivities. Buffy suddenly finds herself dealing with an enemy whose anger comes from something considerably more complicated than an ordinary supernatural grudge. And that's where the episode gets interesting.

Here's a clip from the episode featuring Spike, a resident vampire, making a particularly blunt observation. It illustrates how the show didn't simply take one stance on American history but instead explored several conflicting perspectives. Looking back, that's one of the episode's greatest strengths. It encourages viewers to question the simplified version of history they've grown accustomed to hearing and consider the experiences of people who were often left out of the traditional narrative. Even decades later, there's value in using popular entertainment to introduce these uncomfortable conversations. Episodes like " Pangs " can remind us that understanding history means looking beyond the familiar stories and being willing to acknowledge perspectives that don't always make it into the textbooks.

The timing is worth remembering, too. America was preparing for Y2K, and Britney Spears was everywhere. The Blair Witch Project had turned a walk in the woods into a potential nightmare. Yet Buffy was tackling colonialism during a holiday that most television shows treated as an excuse for sitcom misunderstandings. Hus wants revenge for the violence committed against his people and Buffy has to stop him from killing innocent people. Meanwhile, Angel turns up unexpectedly and creates another headache for the Slayer. It's a strange combination of historical commentary and romantic complications. Somehow, the gang still has to figure out Thanksgiving dinner. Honestly, that's probably the most unrealistic part of the whole episode.

I've always found " Pangs " interesting because it understands that Thanksgiving comes with a rather complicated history. The episode doesn't simply give Buffy another monster to fight. It challenges the traditional story surrounding the holiday and brings Indigenous dispossession into a mainstream supernatural drama. That's a pretty ambitious move for a series that also gave us giant praying mantises and vampires with terrible fashion sense. The problem is that Hus becomes the villain of the week despite having legitimate reasons to be angry. Buffy ultimately has to defeat him to protect her friends. That creates an uncomfortable contradiction at the heart of the story.

There's also the question of how much room the episode gives Indigenous perspectives. The Chumash history provides the conflict but the story largely follows Buffy and her familiar circle of friends. That doesn't erase the episode's willingness to raise the subject. It does make its approach feel limited when revisiting it today. Still, I'd rather see a television series take an ambitious swing and leave viewers with something to discuss than watch another Thanksgiving special where everybody argues about who brought the wrong pie. " Pangs" doesn't get everything right. But it certainly gave Buffy fans something more interesting to remember than another holiday dinner gone wrong. And in Sunnydale, that's saying something.

articles.title: The Center of the News Universe Has Shifted to CNBC
articles.summary: The most consequential stories of this moment in time are happening on the Versant brand, from the stunning fall and rise of Nvidia's Jensen Huang, to Anthropic's IPO.
articles.content:
On Monday morning, CNBC senior Washington correspondent Eamon Javers was driving in his car when the President of the United States called.

Javers pulled over to the side of the road, and within minutes he and President Trump were live on Squawk on the Street to talk about Nvidia 's shock decision to bring back CEO Jensen Huang. Trump was on the show for nearly an hour, revealing his central role in securing Huang's return.

In an interview with The Hollywood Reporter Monday afternoon, KC Sullivan, the president of CNBC, called this morning's coverage of Huang and Nvidia a "really special moment."

"The President was so generous with his time, but it was fun to see Eamon bring that in, and then to have [Jim] Cramer jump in, Sarah Eisen jump in, Carl Quintanilla jump in, David Faber jump in, and to be able to get all those different perspectives, I just think it made such a rich discussion," Sullivan said. "I was really just so proud of the team and how they delivered."

For months, the news business has been focused on the 2026 midterm elections, and for good reason. But the midterms are over, and suddenly it seems the most consequential stories of this moment in time are happening on CNBC.

Nvidia stock soared 31.8 percent on Monday after the news, and the entire stock market rallied. Huang and Nvidia are not only a business story, they are an economic story, a political story, a national security story. It's a story of our time. For CNBC, it was also the second highest hour of web traffic this year, behind only SpaceX's IPO in June.

"In the world of media now, it's those who are essential to their audience and really understand their brand promise and deliver on that are the ones that are going to going to thrive," Sullivan says. "I do think that there's a lot of attention on the business world right now, and I don't think there's anybody who can compete with us in that arena."

For CNBC, that audience includes Trump, as well as seemingly every CEO of note in America. "I want to congratulate you guys. You covered it really well," Trump told the Squawk on the Street hosts during his marathon interview.

Huang, of course, is just the latest news. Last week, it was Cramer's exclusive interview with Nvidia's interim Colette Kress as the company reported its first (and only?) earnings report without Huang at the helm. Two days later Andrew Ross Sorkin had an exclusive interview with Anthropic co-founders Dario and Daniela Amodei as the AI company IPOd.

"It's not like those things just happen. Those are long-term, trusted relationships," Sullivan explains. Eamon has been working that relationship to the President for many months, which put him in a position to do that; Cramer's relationship and trust with Nvidia is what allowed him to get that first interview with Colette; [Joe] Kernen's got a really important, longstanding relationship with the Treasury Secretary so when he was playing a major role over the last two weeks, to be able to have him come on our air; Sorkin has the relationship into Anthropic. Those aren't gimmes. Those aren't just things that happen."

Those moments all delivered double-digit ratings increases for CNBC on linear TV, and secured millions of social views and engagements, where they were shared, analyzed and moved the markets.

"At CNBC we pride ourselves on this, but we're the place that the most influential people go to at the most important times and most important moments," Sullivan says. "I think what it comes down to is that our audience wants to understand what is changing, what does it mean, and what do they do with that information? And that's everything from the midterms to the AI trade. When they're trying to to figure out what's going on, they turn to us. And I think our guests know that as well."

The TV news business can be fickle. General interest brands like CNN and NBC News can benefit immensely when major global news is happening, but tend to be consistent on a day-to-day basis. More partisan-leaning cable news channels like MS NOW and Fox News can rise and fall with the outcome of elections, or how people on the right or left side of the spectrum are feeling.

In the case of CNBC, the news cycle today is simply in their wheelhouse, and it is poised to continue over time as OpenAI weighs its own IPO, and with investigations into Nvidia assuredly coming from Congress (MS NOW may benefit from those too).

The CNBC boom also comes at a good time for the news brand, which is set to launch a new direct-to-consumer offering in the coming months. Sullivan is coy on what that specific offering will entail, but he notes that it will lean into its brand attributes of trust, and the live exclusives that the channel has become known for, be it an exclusive interview with the Amodei siblings, or having the President on the phone for nearly an hour.

"I think that what you'll see when we roll out our direct-to-consumer product early next year is that we're doubling down on that to deliver for the audience where and how they want it, making CNBC more useful and making CNBC easier to interact with and more rich for the consumer where and how they want it, but all built off of the same tenets that you saw today or over the last few weeks."

However, the movie will only be released in 2028, and fans in the U.S. will have to wait even longer for its global premiere. Based on the critically acclaimed […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google It's been more than six years since Sword Art Online released its second season, and the next installment is going to be its anticipated feature-length movie. However, the movie will only be released in 2028, and fans in the U.S. will have to wait even longer for its global premiere. Based on the critically acclaimed light novel written by Reki Kawahara and illustrated by BUNBUN, Sword Art Online made its anime debut in 2012 and became a massive hit. Over the years, the anime has released three seasons, three theatrical movies, anime extras, and even spin-offs. The franchise is still standing stronger than ever as fans are eagerly awaiting updates on the upcoming movie, Sword Art Online Movie: Integral Domain .

It's too soon for the movie to share its full trailer and release dates, but fans already know it's going to be another banger. The movie will follow the original story concept written by series creator Reki Kawahara and is set after the Alicization arc. Although the wait for the anime's return is longer than ever, there are several exciting anime fans can watch in the meantime to fill the void. If you're looking for anime with similar vibes to this classic fantasy, we've got you covered.

If you aren't already familiar with Kawahara's other works, Accel World will be a great starting point. The creator has written a few light novels over the years, out of which three have already received anime adaptations. Accel World has the same video game world-building and the intense moments that fans of Sword Art Online will immediately fall in love with. Unfortunately, even though this anime was released in 2012, it never received the attention it deserved. The story centers around Haruyuki Arita, a middle school student who has always been bullied for his weight.

He finds solace in playing online games, but his life takes a drastic turn after he encounters the school's vice president of the student council, Kuroyukihime, who will surpass all his high scores. She also introduces him to Brain Burst, a program that not only allows its users to accelerate their brain waves, but it also functions as an augmented reality fighting game. Kuroyukihime requests his assistance to get to the top, something Haruyuki finds it difficult to refuse, especially after she helped him overcome the bullies that tormented him.

This underrated isekai never received enough popularity to return with a second season. Although there's no denying that the first season is an incredible journey regardless of the fact that there's no anime continuation. This is yet another survival game where a group of people has been thrown into a world of fantasy that they can't escape from. The survival anime follows a group of strangers who wake up in a mysterious fantasy world with no memories of their past lives.

Unlike the generic isekai shows where the reincarnated or transmigrated characters adapt to their new surroundings quickly, this anime doesn’t shy away from showing the brutal reality of being powerless and unprepared in a completely unknown world. It’s a story of survival as it follows ordinary people who have been thrust into a dangerous world where they must fight monsters for food and money. Their struggles are visceral and slow-paced, emphasizing the weight of every decision while the characters try their best to come out of this dangerous world alive.

This is the newest anime from the creator of Sword Art Online , and it premiered in November 2026. The anime is still ongoing, so you can easily catch up with the episodes in no time. While the series is fairly new, it wouldn't be an exaggeration to say it's easily one of the best anime of the year. It has a much darker tone than Kawahara's most popular work. Not to mention that instead of the characters being trapped in a video game, Devils' Crest blends the virtual reality into the real world, making the situation more horrifying than anything.

The story follows sixth-grade students Yuma Ashihara and his twin sister Sawa. While playing a brand-new virtual reality MMORPG, they realize that their world is being fused with the game. It doesn't take long for the situation to turn from bad to worse as death keeps lurking around every corner, causing chaos and confusion among others. What's worse is that someone Yuma personally knows undergoes a terrible metamorphosis and turns into one of the game's horrifying monsters.

Do you agree with our picks – or have an anime you’d like to recommend that shares similar vibes to  Sword Art Online ? Let us know in the comments below.

articles.title: Marvel’s ‘Avengers: Doomsday’ Won’t Screen for BAFTA, Golden Globes and Other Early Awards Groups to Guard Its Spoilers (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.summary: Earth's Mightiest Heroes will fight Doctor Doom in the latest Avengers installment, but they won't face the first wave of critics and major guilds on the awards calendar. Marvel Studios’ “Avengers: Doomsday” will not screen for awards voting bodies before its world premiere, Variety has learned exclusively, a move designed to protect its theatrical run […]
articles.content:
Earth's Mightiest Heroes will fight Doctor Doom in the latest Avengers installment, but they won't face the first wave of critics and major guilds on the awards calendar .

Marvel Studios ’ “ Avengers: Doomsday ” will not screen for awards voting bodies before its world premiere, Variety has learned exclusively, a move designed to protect its theatrical run by keeping the film’s closely guarded plot turns out of the spoiler ecosystem ahead of its Dec. 18 theatrical release. The film premieres Dec. 14 in Los Angeles, just four days before it opens nationwide. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Oscars: 38 Animated Movies, 104 International Films and 190 Documentaries Make the Eligibility Lists, Setting New Records Two Directors, One Oscar: Can Lord and Miller, Los Javis, Fielder and Oppenheim or the Esiri Brothers Break Through?

The strategy follows a well-worn playbook for event films of this scale, from “Star Wars: The Force Awakens” to “Spider-Man: No Way Home.” But protecting the surprises comes at a cost, with “Doomsday” set to sit out a long stretch of the precursor season as voting windows close before most awards voters have seen a frame. The biggest question is: What does that mean for the Oscars ?

The most consequential window belongs to the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences. Preliminary voting for the Oscar shortlists begins Monday, Dec. 7, and closes Dec. 11, with shortlists in 12 categories announced on Dec. 15, the day after the film’s premiere. Those categories are animated short film, casting, cinematography, documentary feature, documentary short, international feature, live action short, makeup and hairstyling, original score, original song, sound and visual effects. “Doomsday” could factor into as many as seven of them.

Visual effects is where “Doomsday” has the clearest path because of how that race is structured, and the studio’s previous successes in the category (i.e., “Guardians of the Galaxy,” “Black Panther: Wakanda Forever”). Before the official 10-film shortlist is announced Dec. 15, the field is narrowed to 20 semifinalists, a list the Academy does not make public, though Variety has reported it exclusively in past seasons . That list is expected to take shape in the coming days. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Under current Academy rules, the president appoints a chair to preside over an executive committee of active and life members of the Visual Effects Branch. That committee reviews a list of eligible films and, through a series of meetings, selects up to 20 for further consideration. Achievements are judged on “the contribution the visual effects make to the overall production” and “the human artistry and skill, fidelity and technical achievement with which the visual illusions are achieved.”

Crucially, the rules build in flexibility that limits the risk of a major spoiler leak. The executive committee “will request that producers provide opportunities to view their films through advance screenings,” and if a film isn’t available two weeks before the selection meeting, excerpts may be submitted instead. If suitable materials aren’t made available, the committee can deem the film ineligible.

It’s not clear whether Marvel Studios screened the full film for the committee or submitted excerpts. Nonetheless, Variety has confirmed that “Doomsday” was submitted to the relevant Academy branches for consideration, along with the materials required for shortlist eligibility.

In other words, a far smaller group viewing a controlled screening or a curated reel gives Marvel a way to stay in the VFX conversation without exposing its third act to hundreds of voters (The Visual Effects Branch is among the top five largest of the Academy). That matters for a studio that has landed visual effects nominations for “Avengers: Infinity War,” “Avengers: Endgame” and “Spider-Man: No Way Home” but is still searching for its first win in the category.

In Variety’s most recent Oscar predictions , “Avengers: Doomsday” is among the early projected five film visual effects nominees alongside “Dune: Part Three,” “Project Hail Mary” and “Wildwood.”

What remains unclear is whether voters in the other branches where “Doomsday” could compete, including cinematography, makeup and hairstyling, original score and sound, will see the full film before the Dec. 11 deadline.

The rest of the early calendar has tougher hurdles to overcome.

That effectively removes the film from this year’s BAFTA longlist consideration. Round one of BAFTA voting runs from Dec. 4 to Jan. 4.

The Golden Globes are also off the table. Voting in the film categories opens Tuesday, and closes Dec. 4, the same day Critics Choice nominations are revealed. Without a screening, “Doomsday” will be absent from every category, most notably Cinematic and Box Office Achievement, which recognizes films that gross more than $150 million worldwide, a threshold the film is projected to clear with ease.

articles.title: Where to Find GTA 6’s Portal to PS2-Era Vice City & What You Can Do There
articles.summary: Courtesy of Rockstar Games One of the coolest Easter Eggs in Grand Theft Auto 6 is a newly discovered portal that transports you back to the series' past, with retro graphics, music, and characters to discover. For players who loved the PS2 era of GTA, such as GTA 3, GTA: San Andreas, Liberty City Stories and Vice City Stories, […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google One of the coolest Easter Eggs in Grand Theft Auto 6 is a newly discovered portal that transports you back to the series' past, with retro graphics, music, and characters to discover. For players who loved the PS2 era of GTA , such as GTA 3 , GTA: San Andreas , Liberty City Stories and Vice City Stories , this is a must-find secret that transforms Vice City into its older self. While not something that provides an achievement, trophy, or other sort of reward, this blast from the past is one of the oddest and more elusive parts of GTA 6 players are discovering just days after the game's launch.

Like many of the other hidden references in GTA 6 , you'll have to do some exploring to figure out where the PS2 Vice City portal is, and what you need to do to activate it. This Easter Egg is actually a call back to a famous cheat in 2002's GTA: Vice City called LIFE IS PASSING ME BY, a code that allowed players to speed up the in-game clock so that day/night cycles went by much faster. By spelling out this cheat again in GTA 6 at various locations on the map, players can get a blast from the past that goes back multiple PlayStation generations.

The first place where you can start spelling out the Vice City code is in a radio tower within the Key Lento area of GTA 6 's map, a place that either Jason or Lucia can climb up into. Once inside the Badger radio tower, you'll find a small Storage room with a series of substation buttons, a lever, and a TV that shows "Club Malibu" on it, mimicking the same font as GTA: Vice City for sharp-eyed fans. A LPL poster is also in this space, indicating the brand of substations you have to travel to across the map to input the cheat mentioned earlier.

By turning on the power switch in this radio tower, you'll be able to hear a sound effect from GTA: Vice City playing, indicating the start of this side adventure. From here, notice the poster showing a PlayStation 5 in the room, with a message that says "LOSE TRACK OF TIME." This is a clue, referencing the PS2 buttons used for the Vice City cheat — W, A, D, and a dot (.). You might notice that some of the LPL substations have switchboards with prompts like "Press W," "Press D," "Press A", or "Press ."By tracking these PS2 commands with the inputs on a PlayStation controller, we can translate that W means Triangle, D is Circle, A is Square, and L1 is the dot (.).

The first code for LIFE IS PASSING ME BY on PS2 is Circle, Circle, L1, Square, L1, Square, Square, Square, L1, Triangle, Circle, Triangle, indicating a 12 button code. This means that 12 substations need to be visited to spell out the code, with the combination being the pressing of D, D, Period, A, Period, A, A, A, Period, W, D, W in the correct sequence. For example, the second substation you visit should have the letters "iF" outside the building, and a "Press D" button inside to get that part of the code together.

If you're still confused, check out the table below, which should have the location of every LPL substation you need to visit, the button you should be pressing, and the part of the Vice City code you should be looking for outside the substation building:

Fast traveling through taxi services, character swapping, or public transportation will automatically reset this process, forcing you to start over with the first substation. As a result, don't start this process unless you have a fast car you're ready to use to drive all over Leonida, and be ready for this to take some time. Once you hit every button in the right order, you'll get a mysterious text message from an Unknown number, telling you to visit the T.H. Power Station (Reactor 2) between the hours of 7pm and 6am, to reveal the secret you've been wanting to see.

The text that says "U-235-REACTOR2 19-06" is directing you to the T.H. Power Station east of the Hamlet area in GTA 6 , which has a similar lever you used to power on each substation. Pulling this lever with the code from the above steps inputted correctly activates a portal, transporting you to a retro version of Vice City. The graphics here are incredibly similar to GTA: Vice City and GTA 3 , calling back to the PS2 games that helped launch the series into superstar status. Here, you can mingle around what seems to be an exclusive nightclub, which has some familiar faces.

Traveling through what could be the initially teased "Club Malibu," this place has plenty of people, but none more famous than Kent Paul, a main character from GTA: Vice City . This character also appears in GTA: San Andreas , and shows up here in this nightclub in GTA 6 if you head to the bar or upstairs in the area. Interacting with Kent Paul upstairs will trigger a cutscene where another portal appears, taking you back to the beautifully rendered world of GTA 6 fully intact. Doing this will also land you several rewards, including:

Basically, this long journey lets you dress up as GTA: Vice City 's protagonist Tommy Vercetti, who themselves is an homage to characters like Al Pacino's Scarface or Ray Liotta's Henry Hill from Goodfellas . As another bonus, Kent Paul is transported to the GTA 6 world, with actor Danny Dyer reprising his role. A quick phone call from Kent confirms this after you exit the portal, concluding one of the strangest, yet most interesting Easter Eggs players have found for GTA 6 .

What is your favorite cameo or Easter Egg from GTA 6 so far? Let us know in the comments below!

articles.title: Marvel's Doomsday Countdown Just Got Bigger With Real-World MCU Locations Getting Upgraded
articles.summary: The countdown to Avengers: Doomsday is drawing ever shorter, and now, in celebration of the upcoming release, some incredible real-world pop-ups connected to the movie are getting fans even more excited. articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google The countdown to Avengers: Doomsday is drawing ever shorter, and now, in celebration of the upcoming release, some incredible real-world pop-ups connected to the movie are getting fans even more excited. Earlier today, the final Doomsday trailer was released, and with it came a flood of reveals, including confirmation that Bucky and Steve will be reunited , a new look at the return of the X-Men, proof that the fan theory that Steve is really Loki is wrong , and so much more. That alone, with less than one month to go, has boosted interest in the upcoming movie once again.

However, the exciting reveals aren't only taking place on screen. Rather, several real-world locations have been upgraded with myriad Doomsday connections, and the size and scale of them are indicative of just how massive this upcoming MCU installment will really be. Specifically, the Doomsday countdown has begun appearing on various new installations, with some unique twists on what's been done before. Check out glimpses of these new installations and more about them below.

Social media has been abuzz with the news that various real-world locations have begun to feature massive Doomsday countdowns with unique MCU designs, which have popped up in tandem with the new trailer release. Among those that have been photographed and shared online are a huge Shuri/Black Panther mask, which has reportedly appeared in Oakland, California, and a giant Gambit card, which has landed in New Orleans, Louisiana. Presumably, there are more (or there will be), but those are the ones currently making the rounds.

A Doomsday countdown and giant Shuri mask have appeared in Oakland pic.twitter.com/vKexLKhCcm

A massive Gambit card has appeared in New Orleans with the ‘AVENGERS: DOOMSDAY’ countdown. pic.twitter.com/PEFuAil6iG

So far, it seems this unique marketing strategy is working. In addition to the appearances getting plenty of attention online, fans are also responding positively to them in the comments. In response to the post showing Gambit's card, for example, one commenter wrote, "This is actually so f—ing cool holy," and another said, "Promotion on a whole level." It's the latter, in particular, that feels notable. While Avengers movies, of course, always receive plenty of attention and fanfare, Doomsday really does seem to be getting a different level of marketing and promotion. After all, while these new installations are cool, they are far from the first real-world appearance from the movie (for one, there has long been a massive Doctor Doom statue in Japan).

While this hopefully means that Marvel has high expectations for the movie, it also very likely reflects the reality that the movie performing well at the box office and with audiences is critically important. Since Avengers: Endgame , the MCU has seemed to struggle to find its footing, and even with the expectation being that the MCU will get a soft reboot after Avengers: Secret Wars , Doomsday will be a very important step in making sure the MCU has a smooth path forward. If the effort going into the marketing is any indication, though, then this movie is more than primed to be a hit.

What has gotten you most excited about Doomsday thus far? Let us know in the comments down below.

articles.title: David Greaves Says 'Once Upon a Time in Harlem' Is "An Act of Resistance" Against Efforts to Erase Black History
articles.summary: When William Greaves died before completing his Harlem Renaissance documentary, his son David, who had helped to shoot it but had never directed a feature film of his own, stepped in to finish it: "I couldn't imagine anybody else doing it," he tells The Hollywood Reporter.
articles.content:
When the veteran newspaperman David Greaves told people about the film that his father, the legendary documentarian William Greaves , had been trying to complete for decades — the one built around footage of a 1972 reunion of Harlem Renaissance luminaries at Duke Ellington’s apartment — some asked him why anyone would want to watch a bunch of old people sitting around talking. He bit his tongue at the time, but recalled during an interview at the recent SCAD Savannah Film Festival , "I was thinking, 'Oh, yeah, watch this!' Because I knew what those old people were talking about , and how important it was." blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4],[300,251]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories 'Awards Chatter' Podcast Danny Boyle on 'Ink' and Murdoch, the 'Trainspotting' Toilet Scene and How 'Slumdog Millionaire' Almost Went Straight to Video SCAD Savannah Film Festival 'American Doctor' Director on Her Powerful Gaza Doc: "I Wanted to Do Something"

David Greaves has been proven correct by the tremendous reception of that documentary, a one-of-a-kind chronicle of a critical chapter in African-American history, which finally premiered at the Sundance Film Festival in January, screened at the Cannes Film Festival in May back and was released by Neon in October under the title Once Upon a Time in Harlem . Sadly, William Greaves didn't live to see the film's completion — he died in 2014 — but his work was finished by his son, who had been a 26-year-old cameraman at the 1972 gathering, but had never directed a film before. "I couldn't imagine anybody else doing it, frankly," David explained during a post-screening Q&A at Savannah's Lucas Theatre. (He also was one of 10 directors of outstanding 2026 docs who appeared on the fest’s Doc to Watch Panel .)

The fact that it took more than a half-century for the film to come to fruition was largely the result of the perfectionist tendencies of William and his second wife, Louise, David's stepmother, who died in 2023. "They had continued shooting on through the decades," further tracing the history of the Harlem Renaissance, David reports. While he's sorry that his father and stepmother weren't able to see the enthusiastic response to the film from audiences of all ages and races, he also feels that it all happened for a reason: "I think that this film was made to come out now , at a very important time in American history, when [some in positions of power] want to erase Black history," he asserted. "This film is sort of an act of resistance against that."
